title: Maximal Square
summary: In an m x n matrix of 0s and 1s, identify the biggest square composed solely of 1s and provide its area.
statement: In an m x n matrix of 0s and 1s, identify the biggest square composed solely of 1s and provide its area.
constraints: 1–300 rows and columns. Every entry is the STRING '0' or '1'; rows have equal length.
Return the AREA of the largest axis-aligned square made entirely of ones. A rectangle with unequal sides does not qualify; if there are no ones, return 0.
hints: A square ending at a cell depends on smaller squares ending above, left, and diagonally above-left.
At a one cell, the largest ending side is one plus the minimum of those three sizes.
Reuse one DP row and save the old above value as the next diagonal; reset the current size on zero cells, then square the largest side.
Track the diagonal before overwriting its previous-row value. Return area rather than side length.
editorial: A new bottom-right one can extend a square only as far as all three neighboring sub-squares support it. The minimum of their side lengths enforces both borders and the entire interior. A rolling row stores above values while the left value is already updated; a separate variable preserves the diagonal. The independent oracle enumerates square positions and side lengths and directly checks every contained cell. This differs from the existing maximal rectangle problem because both dimensions must be equal.

tests.explanation: The largest all-one square has side length 2, so its area is 4—not 2, and not the area of a larger nonsquare rectangle.
Each one is an isolated one-cell square. The 2×2 region contains zeroes, so the maximum area is 1.
